title: Returning subscriber... they used to be better :(
review: 8/7/24 Edit to Witch Casket reply: I would encourage everyone who is unsure of this to also read the 3-star reviews and below. The feeling that we are getting more and more items that feel like they are from Aliexpress or Temu or just cheaply made in China is repeated over and over. In fact, all my complaints below are repeated many times over. It's not just me, and the over-the-top reply of how 'heartbroken' the makers of Witch Casket are can also be seen repeated in the low-star reviews, which honestly feels a bit like a performance and manipulative rather than sincere. :( I was willing to keep my subscription for a bit longer to see if maybe Witch Casket was just having a few off months, but after reading so many reviews remarking on the same disappointments and loss of quality, I realize it may just be how things are now. Sadly, the dramatic and somewhat unprofessional reply (and then seeing similar replies on many other reviews) tipped the scales for me to just cancel. I hope Witch Casket will actually listen to their customers instead of making excuses and learn from these mistakes. Many of us have loved this brand for many years and have supported them with hundreds and hundreds (thousands?) of our dollars and we have been rooting for them for so long it feels like a big let down when they gaslight us and pretend not to see the same problems we are trying to bring to their attention. For the record, when I received the email from Witch Casket for my feedback, I honestly thought my feedback was just going to be seen by them. I did not realize it was a public review until after, and my comments were meant initially just for their eyes. Now, though, I'm glad it's public. I hope it helps others get a more complete picture before they buy.  Original review:It's clear there is a lot of thought given to the cohesiveness and aesthetic of everything, and I appreciate that. I subscribed to this box couple of years ago for a long while, loved it so much, and then stopped for about a year while I was traveling. I've recently re-subscribed again and I'm finding the newer boxes not as satisfying as they were before. They feel like 'less'. Maybe the same *number* of items, but somehow, I'm a little disappointed each month and not quite 'wowed' the way I was before. The small wooden mortar and pestle, for example, while cute, isn't practical, and feels more like a child's toy than a true Witch's tool. Also, I have a bajillion mortar and pestles, actual heavy-duty ones that work for proper grinding of actual herbs, so it's not even something I'd use even if it was a proper size. One of the highlights I always enjoy are the high quality embroidered or printed drawstring canvas bags- these are treasured and I truly love seeing them show up in boxes, especially when they are large enough for a tarot deck or something else equally substantial. Don't ever stop including these, please!Another one I love are the enameled pins and stickers! These are always a win for me, I love collecting them. Keep those coming!This last month's 'Calming Card Deck' was another big let-down. It gave toxic positivity vibes with sentiments and phrases that sounded A.I. generated. This is not a deck I would ever get any use from. Similarly, the felt bat sewing kit was 'neat' and novel, not something I've ever received in any subscription box (Tamed Wild, Goddess provisions, Witch Box, etc.) so there was something new at least, however again, it felt like a child's craft and while I love to connect to my inner child, it just wasn't a hit for me.One more example of an item that felt like a child's toy, as well as a Dollar Store item (yuk!), was the 'Enchanting Altar Cauldron' that was neither enchanting nor a cauldron. It could maybe skate by as a mini-simmer pot or oil warmer. It looks and feels cheap. :(I truly enjoy the lack of plastic in the boxes. It's one reason I've enjoyed being a subscriber. I strive for zero-waste and appreciate this being valued in packaging. One suggestion I have is to spend less money on the branded boxes and packaging that just gets thrown away and more on improving the quality of the products. The caskets have become full of branded boxes and packaging that gives the appearance of substantial and quality items but strays from that reality and leaves me with a lot of cardboard and paper trash that I can't reuse, and cheap products I just don't want.I realize sometimes that I'm an older more experienced practitioner and many of these boxes are designed to appeal to younger people and beginners, but it does get old when boxes start feeling like a lot of filler and fluff rather than a box filled with practical items I'd actually use. On average, maybe half of the items I'm receiving now in the boxes are items I want to use. That's a lot of wasted money imo.

title: Cheap, Private Labeled products. Not worth the money
review: Ordered a March 23 box and it arrived quickly. I actually just got it today and was extremely let down upon opening. Firstly, the customs declaration sticker lists the value of the box, which came in at 29 GBP. The company claims that the value of each box is at least 50GBP last I checked. The items inside were underwhelming. Cheaply, mass manufactured products that I suspect were privated labeled. There is no mention of any employee names beside the two onwers of this brand. They mentioned the "in house designer" in the monthly pamphlet, but I can't find any mention of artists' names. I paid almost 50 USD for this, and do not feel like I got my money's worth. I highly do not recommend buying from this company. Cheap items that feel geared towards the witchy asthetic vs actual functional items geared towards people who practice. The only good thing about this box was the incense fragrance, but you only get a few sticks, and the description on the box says "honeysuckle and cinnamon" yet the pamphlet says "ginger and cinnamon"? I mean no disrespect to the owners and their craft. The spell sheet I got seems like someone put effort in, but I cannot get behind a box that lies about the value, and then sends out such cheaply made, mass manufactured products with a brand slapped on them. Consumers are not dumb, we can tell this is not worth the money. Immediately canceled my subscription. Really bummed out.Edited to add that the previous responses from the company reps towards negative reviews are unacceptable. They like to claim that they design all of the items and that none are private labelled. Interesting, because in one google search, i was able to find a wooden spoon exactly like the "unique" one sent in this box. All you did was pay someone to poorly engrave a saying on the spoon in question. From what i can tell, this is not a legitimate team of witches coming up with unique and useful items. This is a team of two people private labeling products that fit a theme and putting them in a box to be shipped out. Nothing wrong with that, but you then can't get upset at customers who aren't happy with the value. Customers who know what you're up to, and then say it's our fault because we don't "value the products as highly"Of course we don't! Because they aren't quality products! Your idea is nice and I understand the effot it takes to make these boxes and themes even with private labeled products, but to send us such cheap products is a slap in the face. Your boxes go for 27 GBP in the UK, if I remember correctly. Yet you only value these boxes and content at 29, by your own admission to customs, so you're sending UK members alone a 2 pound value and that's unacceptable. Do better. And don't blame customers for being upset that we figured out your business model and blame us when we aren't the ones ripping people offEdited after the replied. Where did i say you weren't real witches? Nowhere. What I did say is that you guys use private labeled products and mislead because your website literally says you cant find these anywhere else in the world. Well guess what? All it took was a quick google search to find your stuff on wholesale websites that offer personalization. How is that not a lie, when your website says on the landing page that you can't find it anywhere else in the world. Maybe there are more than just two people at this team, but then why not credit your artists and designers with their names in the info booklets? And your reviews may be mostly positive but most consumers aren't gonna go looking for if their products are private labeled or not, they won't question because they trust you as a brand. It's up to you as a company to live up to that trust and misleading people about where you get your products isn't ok. You should strive to do better. But this business model has worked for you for years, as someone on youtube also found evidence of private labelling in your products from 3 years ago. I never called into question your craft's legitimacy, only your business model. I don't appreciate you playing victim.

We ship our monthly witchcraft subscription boxes worldwide! 🌍
 
About
Witch Casket – a family run magickal monthly subscription service, started by a mother and daughter dedicated to bringing a little magick into the lives of others!

Our Mission
Our mission when we launched Witch Casket was to reach witches worldwide…and we are proud to say we have now shipped our magickal witchcraft subscription boxes to subscribers in over 60 countries! It warms our heart to know that there are so many magickal people across the globe! 🌎

Each monthly Witch Casket is carefully curated and packaged with love and care. And we package our branded boxes in simple, unbranded mailing bags for those who wish to keep things private! 💗🌿

As vegans who care about Mother Earth, we are proud to say the following:
•   All products are ethically sourced.
•   All products are vegan-friendly and cruelty-free.
•   We avoid single-use plastics when sourcing our products.
•   We only use biodegradable mailers and compostable packing peanuts.
•   We plant one tree for each Casket sold.

title: I am here to express my disappointment…
review: I am here to express my disappointment with this month’s subscription box. It’s difficult to believe that any time, effort or love was used in the making of this box, as almost every item is hugely disappointing. Let’s start with my favourite (best of the worst) The incense smells like a bin. It smells like a BIN.The intuitive insights oracle cards could’ve been made by a 9 year old and I wouldn’t have been surprised. In fact, a 9 year old can probably do better.The crystal is cheap, the pendant is cheap, the tile symbols are cheap. I was promised quality, and quite frankly, I have been conned. And in case you forgot, the incense smells like the bin.However, what disappoints me the most are the passive aggressive, emoji filled non professional responses to other negative reviews. You are a company. You are going to get things wrong. Improve your quality and don’t be passive aggressive to your reviewers, and you might be okay. Thanks for your time and please don’t send me incense that smells like a bin again,Thank you

title: What happened?
review: What happened?? The boxes value and contents are not like they used to be. I used to love watching everyone get these boxes and they have wonderful customer service but as soon as I signed up in June 2024 the contents are less and less and the value is not there. It is like there is not much care put into the box subscription at all anymore. Please put more in that is useful for not just beginner witches and the same herbs every single month. Everything is like trial size. Nothing is even a normal size, even the crystals are tiny. Not enough items in the box for supposedly £70 which they told me was equivalent to around $80. Definitely not that much no where near in each box. I really hope this lovely company comes back better. They are great people.

title: Overall Bad Experience

However, I needed to contact customer service multiple times as they gave me the wrong tracking number that didn't update at all (I paid a little extra on shipping too for worldwide tracking, so it felt like I was ripped off). The refund for unavailable cards was turned into store credit instead of an actual refund, but they had no problem putting the money back on my credit card.When they finally got delivered, all the cards were all fine as described, though unlike competitors like TCG Republic, none of them were protected in plastic card sleeves. They were held in a couple plastic bags in a small cardboard box.I don't think I'll order from Big Orbit Cards again.

title: Negative roll of the dice with these cowboys
review: Spent ages using system to pick cards for trade in. Spent ages putting them in order. A large number of the cards got rejected for reasons I do not agree with but didn’t get a chance to communicate with anyone.  Received an email saying some of the cards had failed and would be returned at an expense to myself. Cards returned within a cardboard sleeve and all 20 or so cards loose inside a plastic bag with no sleeves on the cards even though they where all rare and some worth decent money with high grades. Some cards returned damaged when they where sent pack fresh. Do not use this service they show a total lack of respect. Reply shows how disrespectful these people are. These cards where not damaged when I sent them, you damaged them. Only one was incorrectly inputted a shiny energy inputed as the wrong age, came in a 2022 pack not a 2023 both having similar value. 5.5% of my trade is more than the average sale of your website guessing from some of the reviews. Copy pasted reply with some added dis respect. No attempt at rectifying the problem just shunning, nice customer service.Second reply: still just arguing with the customer.5.5% is you just trying to shame me and make people belive I’m being petty. 5.5% is irrelevant because it could be of any amount. 1 of the cards you rejected would sell on your website for probably £20, you rejected 5.5% of the total amount of cards because I traded in 140ish cards and you treat the customer like this? I hate to think how you treat someone who only trades in a few cards as you seem to care about the amount so much… want to know the stupidest thing? You kept one of the cards you marked as damaged and sent me back a card(worth more) that you marked as accepted. That’s how legitimate your vetting process is. It’s so pathetic how bad you really are.

review: Although the products themselves are of good quality, they're delivery packages aren't. Twice I have ordered the same Item - a pack of 2 ceramic flowerpots, once from Amazon and once from the Baker Ross Website  - and twice they didn't arrive safely. The first time around both units came shattered, the second time only one of the units came broken. I didn't bother to order a third time... Or ask to return it again for that matter.The packaging really ought to be better so as to more safely secure the items (I wouldn't mind paying a little more for this). As of now, the packaging consists of just a cardboard box with very little styrofoam that doesn't even envelop the items completely. It leaves a lot to be desired.In conclusion, I'd probably only order from them again if the items in question aren't fragile, as it is pretty much a dice roll weather they'll arrive in good condition or shattered.Nothing to say of costumer support though, they were kind and fast in their response.

Both arms have since fallen off the statue due only to environmental vibration (people walking, etc...), and all the fingers have broken off due to the brittle nature of the fabrication medium, which is incredibly upsetting. This was a manufacturing defect that should have been caught by quality control or, at the very least, by Movie Figures. At the time, it was a £600 limited edition figure that I now cannot replace. It is incredibly upsetting to invest that much money in something only to find that poor quality control and shabby manufacturing mean that it is now ruined and devalued.

title: Parcel Force is a shoddy courier. Use Hermes instead.
review: Movie Figures used Parcel Force to deliver the item. I checked the tracking information for my package and discovered that the tracking said that Parcel Force attempted delivery of my package the day before. No note was left saying this. People were in at the time that the attempted delivery supposedly happened. There was a car in the driveway and the delivery person would have been able to see people through the front window. Since it seems that Parcel Force didn't even bother to turn up to the delivery address but marked it as "attempted delivery" on the tracking information anyway, I contacted them. They told me the package had been brought back to the "local" depot, which is miles away and said that I can collect it from there. Since that was unacceptable to me, I asked how to get it "redelivered". They gave me a link to an online form. The date on the card was a required field on the form so I messaged back to Parcel Force saying that I didn't have a date because they couldn't be bothered to leave a card. They just told me to put any date. At no point did Parcel Force apologise during my communication with them. They are a shoddy company and a better one like Hermes should be used in the future. I hope they actually bother to try and deliver my package on Monday now.

review: The seller is a very friendly person (hence the second star), sadly their let down every time by a dreadful courier, Parcelforce.I have over 200 figures, only bought 3 from Movie Figures and had delivery issues each time.Parcelforce don’t deliver to the delivery address, they’ll sneak up and slip a card through the letter box though.Once again, even given the lockdown, Parcelforce claimed to have left the package at a post office, Movie Figures claimed it was still on the driver’s van!After a week of being messed around I asked for a refund, never got one they insisted I wait for delivery. When it finally arrived Parcelforce had clearly been playing football with it and obviously it was damaged. Now Movie Figures want it return to refund, remember after they refused to issue one after a week of failed delivery.I won’t use the company again and until the get a decent courier my advice would be to avoid them, their more expensive than their competitors anyway.Dreadful service with a joke of a courier!Response to reply from seller.This is an accurate review and reflective of events. You were asked to provide a refund after failed delivery and refused, preferring to back your courier’s bad behaviour. During our phone call today you even stated no refund until return receipt, which I could not have satisfied as you hadn’t delivered it at that time.What reviews I post is my choice, check amazon where I have posted numerous positive reviews. If you wish to make this personal I will publish the entire affair; emails, PayPal responses into the public domain. Don’t cast defamatory comments about my character.Negative reviews, by their very nature are more likely to be posted as satisfied customers often don’t bother!You had a week to resolve poor service by a courier you selected. When the goods finally turned up they were damaged. You were paid a not insubstantial sum of money for an item for a collectible item, which final turned up in poor condition.  Those are the facts!And as a result of your attempt to cast me in such a bad light you have lost another star off my review. You know I’m a prolific collector, sourcing items from all over the globe. I run and belong to numerous groups, forums and blogs. I’d be happy to share this experience and your Trustpilot response there.Thank you for continuing to demonstrate how you conduct business, for vindicating me and justifying me feedback.

title: Good product and service from WoW BUT
review: The order was shipped promptly and arrived in good condition, I was pleased with the quality received.  My only complaint is the courier DPD.  I waited in all day and at the appointed time slot I was close to the front door, windows open.  I have a very loud bell and no hearing issues.  I was surprised to receive a text during this time period to say I had been out when he called.  No card through the door or attempt to leave with neighbours.  It was then immediately delivered to a post office in a neighbouring village which is several miles away, despite having one within walking distance.  It was clear no attempt to deliver had been made and this was borne out when I made the trip to collect as it appears same thing had happened to many others.  As an older person with mobility issues this was very inconvenient for me especially as I had paid for delivery.  It was also very annoying to keep getting messages saying I had been out when he called, which was not true.  I also discovered it's virtually impossible to reach a live person at DPD just constantly connected to bots.  A wasted day for me.

title: Fantastic first order for a new hobby.
review: I have only just got into Gunpla, after being an on and off modeller/miniature hobbyist for almost 40 years.  After looking at a number of retailers I chose OEShop after they were recommended by a trusted youtuber (Dave of MSPaints).I placed my first order on a weekend, consisting of 8 various kits and a decal set.  The order was confirmed and ready for RM pickup by Sunday afternoon.  It was collected Monday and delivered in perfect condition on Tuesday.All the kits were nicely packaged into a bubble wrapped block and boxed up.  I appreciate the reuse of random packaging as filler too.I felt like an excited teen again as I unpacked it and checked through the kits, with so many lovely kits to build.  Unfortunately, I then had to split them up, as they are gifts from my family for my Birthday and Christmas.  I do get to keep the bonus Gundam stickers to put on my wet pallette though, so thank you for those lovely extras.I am delighted with the service from OEShop and I already have a growing wishlist of kits to order when I can.Thank you and Merry (soon to be) Christmas.Dave (a different one).

description: OEShop the source to the finest stationery, gift ideas, Gundam, and model kits from Japan
title: They're alright
review: They're alright. They're not as friendly as the other hobby stores (Kikatek, Gunpla Oasis, Forbidden Planet, to name a few), however, but they seem to get the decent stock around if Gunpla is all you need and being friendly is secondary.However, I do love to support hobby stores that I know are worthy of patronizing. It's subjective, but that's where this -1 star is.It's like getting my guitars: I want to support PMT as they're friendly and nice and thus I got my Ibanez, and Schecter guitars from them. With their being canny and approachable with their customers, means they got my money where other music retailers won't. (I mean, would you give your money to a bunch of losers? Like this is why we're all crossed when delivery happens and we dread to know it's RoyalMail handing our parcels, right? They're a bunch of turds and you're left with no choice but to pay them for the delivery or go collect the gunpla yourself in Edinburgh.)Same principle applies here with these gunpla stores. This is a hobby and probably 1% of the population care, and that's why I want to patronize the shop who is worthy enough, and great enough.That said, the stores I would love to patronize didn't have the gunpla I want (Providence Gundam from G-Seed), thus I got that gunpla from them. I could have gotten the Epyon and Tallgeese (both from G-Wing), and the Unicorn's Banshee, but the Providence is enough. I can get the other gunplas from the other friendlier stores.That said, if gunpla is what you need and you just treat these hobby stores like Tesco where you got what you need, then OEshop has enough gunpla stocks even with all this pandemic chain disruption going around.

description: OEShop the source to the finest stationery, gift ideas, Gundam, and model kits from Japan
title: Swift delivery and arrived safely
review: I recently had the immense pleasure of purchasing a Gundam model and experiencing the most exceptional service from a vendor that specializes in the sale and delivery of these iconic mecha models. From start to finish, the entire process was a seamless journey that left me in awe of their efficiency and dedication.From the moment I placed my order on their user-friendly website, I was impressed. The selection was vast, catering to every Gundam enthusiast's tastes, whether they were looking for the latest releases or vintage classics. The website's detailed descriptions, high-quality images, and user reviews provided valuable insights into each model, making it easy to make an informed choice.One of the standout aspects of this service was the speed of delivery. I anticipated a long wait given the size and delicacy of the Gundam model, but I was proven wrong. The seller's commitment to fast shipping was apparent when I received a confirmation email with a tracking number mere hours after placing my order. To my astonishment, the Gundam arrived at my doorstep within just two days, securely packaged and in pristine condition.The packaging was a work of art in itself. The seller had taken extraordinary care to protect the model during transit, using multiple layers of cushioning materials, ensuring that it reached me without a single scratch or dent. They had evidently prioritized the safety and integrity of the purchase.The level of customer service was nothing short of remarkable. I had a few questions regarding the assembly process, and their responsive customer support team addressed my inquiries promptly and comprehensively. This level of dedication to customer satisfaction was truly heartwarming.As a collector and a Gundam enthusiast, I was also impressed by the seller's commitment to authenticity. The model I received was a genuine Bandai product, complete with all the intricate details and high-quality materials that one would expect. I could see that the seller truly values the satisfaction and trust of their customers.In conclusion, my experience with this service was nothing short of flawless. The process from ordering to delivery was swift and secure, and the quality of the product met and exceeded my expectations. I wholeheartedly recommend this vendor to fellow Gundam enthusiasts and collectors who are seeking not only top-tier models but also exceptional service. They have undoubtedly set the bar high for their competitors and have earned my trust and future business.

title: Beware - almost impossible to cancel subscription
review: I signed up for the watercolor subscription and have no complaints for the quality of the products however there are some unusual penalties to cancel the subscription.   About 4 or 5 months in, I decided that this medium is not for me and I did not like it.  Under the assumption that like other subscriptions I could cancel with notice, I sent an email.  Got a form email back thanking me for making contact and I would get follow-up email from them within a short time.  No follow up emails.  I ended up sending 4 more cancellation request over the next 4 months with the same result.  As my emails became more insistent, I got a different form email asking if I’ve gotten the emails they were trying to send me for the cancelation.  Of course, I had not.   I sent another cancelation notice immediately after I was notified they had, yet again, charged me for another box.  I notified them in the email they could no longer charge me.  I then immediately notified the subscription payment servicer that I did not authorize any further payments.  Craftamo then attempted to charge me the next month.  Of course when the payment did not go through I finally got an email from a person that said that they would cancel my subscription for an additional fee since two upcoming boxes were left.  I have asked for the contract that allows the additional fee and if it’s in there, I will have no choice but to pay it.  I am making this review to let people know that if you sign up for a subscription, make sure you are committed to it because it appears almost impossible to cancel.  And it is definitely expensive to get art supplies you won’t use.  I paint with oils and acrylics and thought it would be interesting to try this but this is not a “try it” subscription service.

review: I bought an annual subscription to the Emma Lefebvre Watercolour box and paid $628 for the year, an extravagant birthday purchase but I was thinking that would be the entire cost (as with most annual subscriptions). However a month in, I received another bill for shipping and was told that shipping costs would be an additional charge each month and you never quite know how much this charge will be....so far it's gone from $13 to $16. This essentially brings the total cost to nearly $800 for the year. This for a set of brushes, paper, and a paint palette over the course of the year (4 paints each month). Their ambassadors are basically their customer service since the actual customer service doesn't reply. If they put as much effort in their service as they put in their marketing they would only get 5 star ratings. When the brushes work, they are fine. title: My experience with Empire Medals.
review: In October 2021 I sent my medals to Empire Medals to be court mounted and engraved and told them that I needed them back for Armistice Day. They were returned a few days before and were nicely mounted but when I saw the engraving I was appalled because the engraving looked like a child had scratched it on with a nail. I emailed them immediately and, to be fair, they acknowledged that it had failed their quality control but sent them out as I needed them for the day. There was no note or anything to say that what they had done and said they had forgotten to enclose a note to explain. They asked me to return them for correcting. Due to health reasons I was unable to send them back until January 2022 but had been in constant contact with the guy who was dealing with it and I informed him once I’d sent them. After that things went silent, no acknowledgment of receipt of my medals, no estimate on return date etc. I emailed the gentleman in question multiple times but never received a reply. After having my emails constantly ignored by him for so long I was getting annoyed so last month I emailed the company and made a complaint about the lack of communication and information. I got a reply back from a Ms Renton who apologised and said that it would get dealt with immediately, a few days later I received an email from the guy who had been dealing with my account promising to have my medals returned as soon as possible. Fast forward to 1st April 2022, still nothing. I emailed the company again and complained again, within 12 hours I received a reply from Ms Renton saying “I agree 100%. I can offer my apologies but no excuses. The service you have received has been appalling. Your medals will be returned to you tomorrow with the corrected engraving, you should receive them on Tuesday”.  I can say that I received my medals today as promised and, as a gesture of goodwill, she included a set of miniature medals and along with my full size medals which were mounted in a frame. All I can say is thank you very much to Ms Renton, without your help I think I’d still be waiting. Also for the goodwill gesture which is received with many thanks and appreciation. Due to my experience I have left 3 stars instead of the 1 star I was going to leave. If I could give stars for Ms Renton’s help then it would be 4/5 stars.I had not seen the previous reviews about Empire Medals.com before writing this and was surprised at the number of negative reviews.

title: I’d be careful in choosing Empire…
review: I’d be careful in choosing Empire medals. I bought a single medal with engraving but the engraving was misspelt on checking the order I had spelt my own name correctly ! They said they would replace the medal but as I was sending in my medals to be mounted we agreed to keep the medal and mount it I ordered the mounting service months in advance of Remembrance Day but as per my telephone e conversation they agreed and I wrote on the letter accompanying my medals that they should be ready 31 October . This day came and went with no sign of my medals so I rang the company they hadn’t even started them !!!   They agreed to start them that day but said I was missing a medal ! Oh no they kept the medal that was a replacement ! After much searching for emails and being asked the name of the person I spoke to ( who remembers that months later ) they finally agreed to supply the medal and mounted it with the others . Eventually I received the medals on the very day I was leaving to go to the Cenotaph in London . In summary, I felt properly messed about and got the impression this was a shambolic company  . I had to prove what was agreed on the phone after they made a mistake then when we agreed to get the medals to me by 31 October ( sending them months in advance) and I reminded them in my letter , it didn’t happen . There are many medal mounting services out there this may or may not have been a one off occurrence for this company but I’d think twice before using them

title: Company under stress?
review: This company appears to be struggling a bit in recent months. Their website said there was a six-week turnaround for mounting medals, so I ordered a do-it-yourself mounting kit a couple of weeks ahead of November's Remembrance parade, and my payment was taken. I heard nothing for a week and a half, so I followed up, reminding them that I only wanted a do-it-yourself kit (brooch, loose lengths of ribbon and fixings), so no six-week mounting turnaround required from them. I received what I assumed was a generic email, reminding me of the six-week period for medal mounting and telling me that they were experiencing a heavy work load due to Remembrance and recent release of Coronation Medals, and asking me to refrain from following up on orders. Six weeks after placing the order, I had heard nothing more, so I emailed to cancel the order and ask for a refund. Two days later, most of my order arrived, missing one item, but including an printed invoice/despatch note showing the full order. As of 12 December I have had no further explanation.

title: Customer service needs to be more polite
review: Recently ordered jubilee medal ribbons. After waiting 8 weeks with not a single email saying why the delivery was taking longer than 28 days I emailed to ask if there was any update. title: Deliver quickly but delayed refunds
review: Placed my order on 11/12/24 and it did arrive quickly. I had to return the wool due to an error I made, not the company. Wool was received by The Knitting Network on 16/12/24. I waited a few days and since then have sent 4 emails asking when I can expect my refund. Replies have been very quick and I do understand that with the holidays things can get delayed and everybody has been busy but from the email replies I do think my refund could have been looked into and when I could expect it. Hence only 3 stars given. As of todays date I have still not received a refund.

I am pleased with my purchase just not happy at all about onward services.

The knitting network need to be clearer UPFRONT about what materials the needles are made from, and not just relegate this information to the ‘small print’ section of the page!! Due to the cost of postage it is not worth returning these. Will stick to purchasing my supplies from the Wool Warehouse in future.

review: The model is, in places, poorly assembled, presumably by Rapido Train's manufacturer with particularly unsightly gaps where the steam pipes connect to the cylinders, and the joint where the chimney upper half locates. The whistles were askew and one was loose, needing careful re-fixing. The weathering by TMC is why I chose this particular model and is quite good overall but in a few places paint had scuffed off the body revealing the metal underneath, again easily fixed but shouldn't have needed to be. The smokebox was entirely matt black and the limescale staining on in the steam pipe area was clumsy, unsightly, and had got onto the buffer beam area. I have been able to address these issues myself but was disappointed that I felt it necessary.

title: Poor communications & difficult to deal with
review: Wanted customisations including one that wasn't on their website (so couldn't be added to web order). Told by email they could do that. But when I asked them how to proceed and pay, silence.Tried again, when they announced a new customisation available for loco I'd ordered, and which they were still working on, and was told they hadn't got parts and had no idea when they get them.But apart from that, no updates as to where my loco was in the process, until I got the delivery advice.Then, when it did finally arrive, it was in the thinnest cardboard box any model shop has used for posting anything to me. So thin, that it had split, but thankfully the Royal Mail took care of it, and it arrived undamaged. Better packaging for expensive, delicate goods would be better.Weathering requested was competently done.  Maybe you have to pay the premium for Deluxe Weathering over Heavy Weathering to get something really impressive?One final thing that leaves a sour taste, is that I asked for crew to be fitted to my diesel. £15 for one figure feels a bit steep, given that it's the same price for fitting crew to a steam loco, which is surely two figures?  Maybe the extra cost for diesels it to reflect the time taken to open it up to fit them?  They could, however, make that clear, e.g. by saying how many are in the "crew."  And anyway, why the extra charge if they're already fitting a decoder/stayalive?  Just a bit of clarity would have cleared up that sour taste.Very unlikely that I'll use them again.

A set of nuts, to bolt the mini bolts into, would have been nice too.I know it's not the shop's fault. title: These are tribute coins, not issued by Royal Mint
review: I won't go as far as saying they're deceptive, but they should certainly make clearer that many/most of the sovereigns they offer are not issued by the Royal Mint, and are therefore not even legal tender (as Royal Mint sovereigns technically are). The coins are simply what are known as "tribute coins". However, for the prices they charge one could be forgiven for thinking they are "legitimate" coins. Buy tribute coins if one must, but be clear that they are not official British coins of any description, and I can't imagine any serious coin collector being remotely interested in them.

description:

title: 3 way patchbox
review: I purchased the three-way patchbox for organizing cables out of my pedalboard to my amp. This model has 3 jacks: Amp Send, Amp Return and Amp Out (or amp in depending how you look at it. Its the cable that goes from your pedalboard to the input of your amp).I was dissapointed that when using a non-fx loop amp, I am not able to use the patchbox “amp return” jack to go to the amp input without connectic a patchcable that connects the “amp out” jack to the “amp send” jack. It’s the only way to have all pedals in chain in the event that the venue has a non-fxloop amp, for example. This wasn't mentioned in the info available on the website.Most patchboxes I have seen in this price range do not require this extra patchcable for this scenario, and they can do that “bridge” internally.Other than that, everything works great. You have a lot of options for customization and maling the product “yours”.

title: Delivery prompt - not sure about the service
review: No problem at all with service in terms of communication and delivery, my order arrived on the day and reasonably early. Three star description mentions friction between buyer and selIer. In this case it is not true.I photographed the outside packaging on delivery, which had slight damage/hole on one corner but assumed that it would be outer packaging; it was.When I took out the box from inside there was a hole through which I could see the pickup switch. Inside the box was the protective cover that had not been fitted. There was no damage to the switch. At first I thought one of the volume dial was bent but found that it was loose and not fitted correctly. Removed it and pushed fully on and straight. There was a drop down menu when I ordered to select a free gift. I opted for a setup worth £35. I guess I should have gone for something I could see, such as a tuner as there was no mention of this on the receipt that came in the box. Not sure my guitar received the setup as I assume the ill fitting dial would have been noticed. Guitar looks and sounds nice but small things leave you wondering whether I would order again in the future.

title: A little disappointing...
review: After exchanging several email enquiries and a phone call, I finally decided to purchase a Martin GPC-13E. I asked for a low-action set up and Elixir strings (just don’t like the Martin brand of strings). Guitar was dispatched with next-day delivery expected with DHL. My tracking App said they had collected the parcel but when I checked the next morning (looking for a delivery time slot), tracking said delivery was delayed for delivery on next working day. No reasons were given. Hugely disappointing. Guitar arrived the following day. Lucky it did as this was a Friday and had it not arrived, the next working day would shift to the following Monday. This is somewhat at odds with the delivery policy on the vendors website. I’ve had issues of this kind with DHL in the past. Best courier by a mile is DPD. Guitar was well packaged with outer box, some bubble-wrap and a padded soft shell case (branded). No obvious damage and when opened, all was ok. Guitar is a lovely instrument-but so it should be. It’s a Martin and not cheap (over £1300). Setup was completed although perhaps the action could have been a tad lower. All ok. The Martin branded soft shell case is in my opinion, average at best. Yes it’s padded a little better than a cheaper gigbag  but I was expecting better for the price. My disappointment centres around the “package”. For this money, I was hoping for some included accessories eg. Cleaning products, strap, etc. I know none of this is included in the website description - but neither was the gigbag. Back in January’21, I bought a Gibson G series acoustic from PMT. That came with a quality hard-shell branded case and included accessory pack (standard according to Gibson’s official site) and all at a cost £450 less than this Martin. Perhaps I was naive in thinking Martin would offer similar or a vendor would add accessories to make the product more attractive. I am not looking for “freebies” but the comparison was stark with such a cost differential. I sent an email to Steven James Guitars to check nothing had been left out, but as yet, there’s been no response. I considered strongly how to rate my experience. Whilst staff were very nice and responded promptly to my enquiries pre-purchase, nothing since.  Hence, with the delivery issues added in, I went for 3 stars. I do not plan to return the product (unless a fault develops). So I’ll just leave it there. It’s always going to be difficult to purchase a guitar online without playing it first, but this is where customer service becomes paramount. I have no comments on recommendation.

title: Disappointed.
review: I ordered a brand new Fender Cabronita Telecaster (Blonde Ash) and when it arrived it was clearly not 'brand new' and factory fresh. It looked like it had been played a lot; it was covered in light scratches and had a couple of dark marks in the finish? But, worst of all it had two bad dings. One of the dings on the edge of the guitar had some sort of yellow filler in it? I phoned the shop and the guys at the shop organised a return straight away and emailed me the label to print-off. The guitar got picked-up a couple of days later and was returned to the shop without a hitch, at no extra cost to me. Once it had arrived, they phoned me the next day and I got a full refund without any hassle. They sent me two sets of strings to make up for it but it cost me two wasted days. What was annoying, is that this guitar was supposed to be inspected, restrung and have a full "expert set-up" before leaving the shop. Either, it didn't have one or the guitar technician was having a really, really bad day? I'm no expert, but I've been playing guitar for 40+ years and I could tell that the guitar was not right. The guys at Steven James Guitar & Amp were very friendly and helpful and very quick to put things right, but the fact remains, this guitar should've never been sent out in the first place. I hope it's a one-off.

title: Used Lefthand ESP Viper 100FM
review: I purchased this guitar after seeing it online described as in excellent condition. The member of staff who aided me was very helpful, and the item was well packed when it arrived. Upon receiving the instrument I was quite disappointed. I like the guitar, but the condition is anything but excellent. I would have described it as good at best. It had several scratches & dings in the body, including two dents at the bottom of it where it appears it was bashed against an amp. Anyway, I have spent the last few weeks correcting these flaws. When I removed the strings there are also scratches on the pickups. The Truss rod had to be adjusted, but the neck could have moved in transit. There was some buzzing at the first few frets, so adjusted the Truss Rod to acquire some relief in the neck. Problem fixed. I wanted to give a positive review, but the item condition is not as described. I like the guitar very much, so been working on it to restore it to almost new condition. Have two Dean USA pickups to install too. I've been playing guitar & buying them for almost twenty years, and I think this is the most misleading product I've purchased in that time. A guitar should not be advertised as excellent condition when it is in fact only good. The photograph did not show any of the blemishes. Although some of the customer service was decent, the item is not as described. Buyers beware!
